CodeCatalog

Penfold · 11 desktop and 13 mobile screens, every one live HTML and CSS rather than a picture of it. The desktop set was rebuilt from raster exports and squared up into one flow; the mobile set was read from the Figma file. Pick a screen, compare it with what it was built from, or lift it out whole — each lives in its own folder with a drop-in embed.

Notes

The first screen of the whole set, and the only one at 1231 wide. One image arrived — state five of six, with the third section open — and it was measured and built on its own. The other five states were then written from it, which the flow layout makes cheap: opening a section pushes everything below it without a single position changing. The live version folds all six back into one full-height page with a working accordion, all three sections closed to start. The code pane here shows state five, the one that came from the picture.

Two different jobs

The desktop screens had no design file behind them — only pictures. Sizes, colours and positions were measured out of the pixels and verified by re-rendering. The mobile screens came from the Figma file, so their values are exact; the work there was catching where the file’s own model and the browser’s disagree.

The typeface, corrected

The desktop screens were first built in Figtree, a fitted match. They are now all Montserrat, which the Figma file uses for mobile and which the pictures confirm: measured against three separate headings, Montserrat lands within 1.4% of the source and Figtree is 9–19% too narrow. The old sizes had been inflated about 12% to fake that missing width, so they came down with it — 55px to 49, 22px to 19.4.

The shared shell

Across the desktop set: column at x 183, measure 770, heading top 92 at 49px/57px with -0.9px tracking, paragraphs 19.4px/29.5px 23px apart, body copy the same navy as the headings. Each screen's own internal spacing was left as measured and shifted whole, so nothing inside a screen changed rhythm.

Live, but not clickable here

Each build is embedded in its own shadow root so 24 stylesheets can share one page without colliding. Their scripts are left out, so the multi-state screens show one state each — the links above open the clickable versions.
